extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys and agents) and counsel who practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing practitioner conduct before the USPTO (notification obligations, conflicts, client withdrawal, third‑party payments) and the sanctions/processes the Office may impose (reprimand, probation, suspension, publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify Director in writing of change in professional licensure status
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent knowingly failed to notify the Director in writing of his change in his professional licensure status that would preclude continued registration as a patent attorney under 37 C.F.R. § 11.6 (violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(14)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must timely notify the OED/Director in writing of any change in state licensure status that would affect continued registration as a patent attorney; failure to do so constitutes conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice. (Example fact pattern: Respondent remained registered as a patent attorney despite suspension by State Bar of California and only changed status after OED notification.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not hold out authorization to represent trademark matters while not licensed
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing to hold oneself out as authorized to represent clients in trademark matters before the Office while not licensed to practice law by the relevant State Bar violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.31(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To represent clients in trademark matters a practitioner must be an attorney who is a member in good standing of the highest court of a State (see 37 C.F.R. § 11.1 and § 11.14). Practitioners suspended from state bars must cease representing clients in trademark matters and change status (e.g., to patent agent) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely withdraw from representation when client sues the practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Not timely withdrawing from representing a client after the client brought suit against the practitioner violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.40(b)(4) (referenced as § 10.40(b)(4) / § 10.40).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a client sues the practitioner, the practitioner must promptly withdraw from representation before the Office; continuing to act for the client in prosecution after being named in litigation is improper (example: Respondent continued prosecution of the '032 application after Ms. C sued, and only filed a Request for Withdrawal years later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting employment only with client consent after full disclosure (third‑party payments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting employment without the consent of the client after full disclosure, where the exercise of the practitioner's professional judgment may be affected by the practitioner's own financial, business, property, or personal interests, violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a third party (e.g., invention development company) pays or stands to pay for legal services, the practitioner must make full disclosure and obtain the client's consent; failure to disclose payments or to obtain client consent is prohibited. (Fact example: Respondent accepted compensation routed by ISC without Ms. C's consent after full disclosure.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline proffered employment when independent judgment likely impaired
rubrics_metrics.description: Not declining proffered employment where the exercise of the practitioner's independent professional judgment on behalf of a client will be or is likely to be adversely affected by acceptance of the employment (or where it would likely involve representing differing interests) violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.66(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must assess whether accepting representation would compromise independent judgment or create conflicting interests; if so, they must decline the employment rather than proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent multiple clients only when adequate representation and consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing multiple clients where it is obvious the practitioner cannot adequately represent the interests of each, and/or representing multiple clients without first obtaining the consent of each client after full disclosure, violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.66(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent representation of multiple clients is permitted only when adequate representation for each is possible and each client gives informed consent after full disclosure of possible effects on the practitioner's independent judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting compensation from someone other than the client requires consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting compensation from one other than the practitioner's client for the practitioner's legal services to or for the client without the consent of the client after full disclosure violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third‑party payments must be fully disclosed to the client and the client must consent; otherwise the practitioner's acceptance of such payments is improper. (Example: payments from ISC to cover Ms. C.'s patent services without her informed consent.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice law
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice law (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)) — the general standard under which specific violations (e.g., failing to notify licensure change) are characterized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The umbrella fitness standard covers acts and omissions that undermine a practitioner's integrity, competence, or standing. Specific breaches of rules (notification failures, conflict management failures, misrepresentation of status) can be charged under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available and imposed: public reprimand and probation terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order publicly reprimanded the respondent and imposed a sixty‑month (60‑month) probationary period; respondent is permitted to practice before the USPTO during probation unless suspended by order of the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions can include public reprimand and probation with conditions. The order imposed obligations (notify the affected client within 30 days, provide OED an affidavit within 45 days) and sets compliance monitoring during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED enforcement process during probation: Order to Show Cause and suspension recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED believes the respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or disciplinary rules during probation, OED shall issue an Order to Show Cause, grant 15 days to respond, and may deliver materials to the USPTO Director requesting immediate suspension for up to sixty (60) months (see procedural steps in Final Order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED follows a defined sequence: issue Order to Show Cause, send to respondent, allow 15 days to respond; if OED remains of that opinion, deliver the Order, response, and supporting evidence to the USPTO Director and request suspension. Requesting review of suspension does not stay or postpone an immediate suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of suspension: dissociation from customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspended, the USPTO shall promptly dissociate the respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates; the respondent shall not use or obtain USPTO customer numbers or PKI certificates unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension triggers technical and access consequences to prevent practice before the Office: removal of identifiers and credentials, and prohibition on obtaining or using such credentials until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Public Reprimand and Probation (and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions are publicly posted in the OED Reading Room and formally announced in the Official Gazette; the notice must state the discipline and the rules violated as in the sample notice included in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement/agreement caveats: Office may pursue further discipline and consider settlement in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the settlement or Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57 for the misconduct that caused immediate suspension, nor from considering the settlement or Final Order in future complaints as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement does not immunize the practitioner from subsequent discipline for the same misconduct; the Office may use the settlement as evidence or an aggravating factor in later proceedings. Parties bear their own costs unless otherwise stated.
